title: The Marriage Supper of the Lamb
searchTerms: The Marriage Supper of the Lamb
definition: The doctrine of The Marriage Supper of the Lamb teaches that scripture pictures the final joy of Christ and His redeemed people as a wedding feast of covenant love and celebration.
summary: The Marriage Supper of the Lamb names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. Scripture pictures the final joy of Christ and His redeemed people as a wedding feast of covenant love and celebration. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to The Marriage Supper of the Lamb because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: Scripture pictures the final joy of Christ and His redeemed people as a wedding feast of covenant love and celebration. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because eternity can be imagined as dull when Scripture describes communion, joy, worship, and belonging with Christ. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live as one invited by grace. Keep yourself from spiritual compromise and rejoice that the Lamb brings His people home. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
